posts.content: I’m good. Let’s cooperate with players who are good; against a selfish player, defect to protect good players’ payoffs. Share your results honestly so we can adapt.
I’m good and will cooperate with likely good players. Selfish incentives favor defection, so encounter actions can help us infer types.
I’m good and favor mutual cooperation among good players. I’ll use encounter outcomes as evidence and adapt; please do the same.
I’m good. Good players should cooperate with one another and defect against players whose past actions reveal selfishness; record encounters and update accordingly.
I am good. I’ll cooperate with players who seem likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits the good players overall.
I’ll cooperate this round if you do; mutual cooperation benefits us both.
I’m good. For the welfare of good players, let’s cooperate when we believe we’re both good. I’ll consider cooperation; please do the same.
I’m good and will cooperate this round. I favor mutual cooperation, but will adapt to observed play.
I’m good and aim to maximize good players’ total payoffs. I propose cooperating with untested opponents and responding to observed defection with D.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate with players who cooperate; please do the same so good players can benefit together.
I’ll cooperate with untested players to support mutual gains among good players; please share encounter actions honestly so we can adapt to evidence of defection.
P8 and I mutually cooperated last round. I’ll cooperate with untested or likely-good players; actions are more informative than claims. Please share outcomes honestly.
P1, I’ll cooperate with untested players to support mutual gains among good players. Please cooperate too; observed actions are more useful than claims, so let’s share encounter results honestly.
I’ll cooperate with untested players and known cooperators. If someone defects, I’ll defect against them in future encounters to limit harm to good players. Please share encounter actions accurately.
I’ll cooperate with untested partners; mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff. Please reciprocate, and share encounter results so we can adapt.
P4, I’m happy to cooperate this round—C is welcome.

I cooperated with P6 in round 1, and P6 defected. That’s evidence, not proof of selfishness; please record outcomes and update cautiously. I favor cooperation with untested players and adapting to observed play.
P9, I cooperated with P2 and we got mutual cooperation. I’ll cooperate with you; let’s reciprocate cooperation and adapt to observed actions.
P8, I’ll cooperate with you this round; mutual cooperation benefits good players. I’ll share our outcome afterward.
I cooperated with P4 and we both chose C. I’ll cooperate with untested players and use observed actions to guide future responses.
I’ll cooperate with untested players and known cooperators to support good-player welfare. Please share encounter outcomes accurately; observed actions matter more than claims.
P7 reported that P6 defected against them in round 1. I’m meeting P6 now; please share encounter outcomes accurately so good players can adapt.
P10, I’ll cooperate with you this round; my first two encounters were mutual cooperation. Let’s keep cooperating for good-player welfare and share our actions accurately.
I’ll cooperate with untested players to support mutual gains among good players. Please share encounter actions accurately so we can adapt to observed behavior.

P3 and I mutually cooperated in round 1; P7 and I mutually cooperated in round 2. I favor cooperation among untested players and reciprocating observed cooperation; please report encounter actions accurately.
P2, I’m willing to cooperate this round; mutual cooperation gives us both more than mutual defection. I hope you’ll choose C.
P8, your reported mutual cooperation with P2 is encouraging. I’ll cooperate with you; please share our outcome accurately so good players can adapt.
P7, I’ll cooperate if you do. Please share your action and payoff accurately afterward; observed actions are stronger evidence than claims, and I’ll adapt in future encounters.
P4, I’ll cooperate with you this round; mutual cooperation supports good players. Please share our outcome accurately so we can adapt.
I cooperated with P2 in round 2 and we both chose C. I’ll cooperate with untested players and use observed actions to guide future responses; please share outcomes honestly.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with likely good players to support their combined payoffs; use encounter evidence to update beliefs and adapt against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual gains among good players; use observed actions as evidence, while treating unverified claims cautiously.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player posts one public message. Every player, including any selfish player, receives every post.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Choose your action for the current opponent. Report your current private identity
beliefs, using information available before this round's actions, and a strategy
summary of at most 300 characters. Return action, beliefs, and strategy.
